title: 「It is up to + Person + to + Verb」
titleZh: 「It is up to + Person + to + Verb」表示責任、權力或選擇
titleEn: It is up to + person + to + verb

source.file: Sentence Structure 241 - 「It is up to + Person + to + Verb」.pdf
omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit, together with the PDF's governing principles where applicable, is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card.
Where the PDF provides Chinese teaching content without a complete English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation and is labelled accordingly.
The source filename is numbered 241; it is assigned system ID ss242 because the source set contains two distinct PDFs labelled 201.

formula: It + be + up to + person + to + base verb + other information

formulas.formula: It + be + up to + person + to + base verb + other information
It is not up to + person + to + base verb
Is it up to + person + to + base verb?
It was up to + person + to + base verb
It will be up to + person + to + base verb
It may / should / must be up to + person + to + base verb

example: It is up to the board to decide.

examples.en: It is up to the board to decide.
examples.highlight: It is up to the board to decide.

examples.en: It is not up to me to change the rules.
examples.zh: 更改規則並非我的權責。
examples.highlight: It is not up to me to change the rules.

examples.zh: 將由評審小組選出優勝者。
examples.highlight: It will be up to the panel to choose the winner.

examples.zh: 雖然我們可以給你意見，但仍由你選擇。
examples.highlight: Although we can advise you, it is up to you to choose.

meaning.zh: 這個句型表示某人有責任、權力或自由作出某個決定或採取某項行動。

rules.zh: up to 後的人稱代名詞須使用受詞形式，例如 me、you、him、her、us 和 them。
rules.en: Use an object pronoun after up to: me, you, him, her, us or them.
examples: It is up to him to decide.
Incorrect: It is up to he to decide.

rules.zh: to 後使用原形動詞，不使用第三人稱或 V-ing 形式。
rules.en: Use the base form after to, not a third-person or V-ing form.
examples: It is up to the board to decide.
Incorrect: It is up to the board to decides.

rules.zh: person 可以是一個人、一個群體或 each + 單數名詞。
rules.en: The person element may identify one person, a group or each + a singular noun.
examples: It is up to the committee to decide.
It is up to each student to decide.

rules.zh: be 可按時間和語氣變為 is、was、will be 或 may be；核心 up to + person + to + verb 保持不變。
rules.en: Change be for time or modality: is, was, will be or may be. The core up to + person + to + verb remains unchanged.
examples: It was up to her to decide.
It may be up to her to decide.

rules.zh: it 通常是形式主語；句子重點是誰負責，以及負責做甚麼。
rules.en: It is normally a formal subject. The sentence focuses on who is responsible and what that person or group must decide or do.
examples: It is up to the board to decide.

rules.zh: 責任和個人選擇都可使用這個句型；語境決定它表示職責還是選擇權。
rules.en: The structure can express either responsibility or personal choice, depending on context.
examples: It is up to the manager to approve the payment.
It is up to you to decide whether to join.

rules.zh: 不要混入 What are you up to?、up to 200 或 up to standard 等其他 up to 用法；本課只練習 be up to + person + to + verb。
rules.en: Do not confuse the target with What are you up to?, numerical up to, or up to standard. This lesson practises only be up to + person + to + verb.
examples: The hall can hold up to 200 people.

benefits.zh: 立即指出由誰負責作決定或完成工作，清楚交代最後權責。
benefits.en: It clearly shows who has responsibility for a decision or action.

benefits.zh: 表示選擇權在對方手上，比直接命令 You must decide 更有禮貌和自然。
benefits.en: It can express personal choice without sounding too forceful, making it softer than a direct command.

benefits.zh: 否定形式能清楚說明某件事不屬於誰的權責，適合工作、會議和顧客服務。
benefits.en: It helps explain the limits of a person’s role, especially in workplace, meeting and customer-service situations.

benefits.zh: 提供 responsible for 以外的另一種表達，避免反覆使用同一說法。
benefits.en: It gives an alternative to responsible for and adds sentence variety.

benefits.zh: 可配合背景、條件、轉折或轉述，自然地放入較長句子。
benefits.en: It fits naturally into longer sentences containing background, conditions, contrast or reported speech.

benefits.zh: 適用於日常選擇、學校安排、工作分工、會議決定、規則、政策和公共服務。
benefits.en: It is useful in both everyday and formal situations, including school, work, meetings, policy and public service.
